text:
maria: Kicked off a private/VPC canary to acme-staging and the control-plane bundle never reached the edge nodes in the air-gapped site. Not seeing the new split or the canary guards applied. Anyone seen this pattern before?
	dan: Ugh. Is this the signed bundle propagation or the heartbeat ack issue?
	maria: Looks like bundle uploaded to customer s3 proxy, control-plane marked DONE, but edge nodes report last_seen=0. We have no pull logs.
	tina: If it's air-gapped, nodes pull on a schedule. When did the bundle become available?
	maria: 1951234400 according to control plane. Nodes poll every 15m by default for private deploys. Could be we missed a window.
	ryan: Did the canary traffic split get applied in the route table or only in the control-plane config?
	maria: only in control-plane config. The route table stays unchanged until nodes ack the bundle.
	deploy-bot: [deploy] canary 2026-03-19T14:00 started -> canary-id c-9f3a, target 5% traffic, guards=latency,errors.
	dan: For air-gapped customers we should probably fallback to a local staged rollout if nodes don't ack within X. Right now it's all-or-nothing which is causing long waits.
	maria: Agreed. Proposal: if no ack after 3 polling windows (45m) mark canary as "degraded-pull" and flip nodes that have the bundle to accept 1% traffic via local rule, keep others at 0. That reduces blast but lets us test in-situ.
	ryan: How do we detect "have the bundle" without changing node agent? We only see heartbeats, not bundle hash.
	tina: We can add a simple health endpoint on node-agent that returns last_bundle_hash and last_applied_ts. Should be small change and backwards compatible (returns empty string on old agents).
	maria: Would prefer avoiding agent change for quick mitigation. Alternative: edge nodes could emit a tiny metric when they start Nginx/proxy with new config. We already ingest metrics for private via pull.
	dan: Metric approach is fine but pulls need config to be applied first. Chicken and egg.
	ops-bot: incident note: customer acme-staging reported rollout delay at 2026-03-19T14:45.
	maria: For short-term: I'm going to add a control-plane heuristic: if bundle uploaded but no node_pull within 30m, create a signed "kick" artifact and mark the canary as "kick-recommended" in console (manual action). Console shows a big amber banner.
	ryan: Can we automate the kick for small canaries (<2% traffic) with an opt-in org policy? Some customers accept remote kick for faster recovery.
	maria: Yes, add org-level opt-in flag: "allow_remote_pull_kick". Default off. Will surface via API + console toggle.
	tina: UX note: console should show which nodes acknowledged and which haven't, with last_seen, last_bundle_ts, and an action button to send the kick.
	dan: Also add a canary guard: don't go to 5% unless 3 nodes (or N% of nodes) have acknowledged. For tiny fleets N=1. For larger fleets N=3. Keeps safety.
	maria: Implementation plan: (1) short-term manual kick artifact + console banner; (2) mid-term metrics/agent field for last_bundle_hash; (3) long-term opt-in auto-kick + guard thresholds per org.
	ryan: Logging: when a kick is sent, add an audit entry with bundle_id, operator, and signature so customer can validate.
	maria: Agree. Also we need a fallback API: /v1/private/canary/{id}/status that returns computed state (pending, degraded-pull, partially-applied, applied) so external automation can react.
	dan: One more thing: quota and billing. If we flip a small portion of traffic locally, do we count tokens as charged to customer host or to the hosted pool? Need to ensure billing attribution stays correct.
	maria: Good catch — billing must remain on-customer for private. We'll ensure metrics pipeline tags origin=private-edge when local rule applied.
	tina: I'm going to sketch the agent minimal change for last_bundle_hash and a lightweight /agent/status endpoint. If we can do that in a single minor release we can retire the manual kick in 6 weeks.
	deploy-bot: [deploy] patch release planned: agent v2.3.1 -> includes /agent/status. Scheduled 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC.
	maria: Thanks. Action items: Tina to PR agent status; Dan to add console banner and kick UI; Ryan to add API endpoint; I'll add audit entries and the canary state machine.
	ryan: I'll own the API and add the org opt-in toggle in the config schema.
	dan: I'll prototype the guard threshold logic and put a draft in the design doc.
	maria: Great. I'll notify customer about manual kick option and timeline. If anyone sees a better quick workaround ping me. :thumbsup:
